title: AI-Native Organisations Run on Skills: How to Structure and Scale Them — Imad Touil, QuantumBlack
talk_summary: Imad Touil argues that agent workflows are only as deterministic as their skills, and that skills must be treated like microservices: modular, discoverable, versioned, composable, and governed via a central registry. He shows a simulation where ungoverned skill sprawl causes duplication, quality decay, and token waste, and proposes a centralized skills catalog with metadata, MCP/CLI access, access control, and evals.

takeaways.technique: Centralized skills registry with metadata and versioning
takeaways.what_they_do: Maintain one searchable catalog of skills with owner, dependencies, version, lifecycle, and access control; agents pull the latest version at runtime via MCP or CLI instead of each team reinventing prompts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need a centralized platform that have a catalog with metadata in it that's actually can discover skills and could be searchable

takeaways.technique: Progressive disclosure of skills to cut context
takeaways.what_they_do: Load only the right skills at the right time rather than stuffing all know-how into the system prompt, explicitly to reduce token usage.

takeaways.technique: Static skill linting against best practices
takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate skills statically against Anthropic's skill best practices (structure, invocation clarity) as a cheap proxy for quality before runtime evals exist.
takeaways.evidence_quote: test like you you l static test your or evaluate your skills against the entropic best practices

takeaways.technique: Composable domain skills for deterministic review workflows
takeaways.what_they_do: Compose small specialized skills (retention policy, GDPR rules, disclosure standards, templates) that a review workflow pulls automatically, producing deterministic audit output instead of ad-hoc prompting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this gets pulled automatically by on the runtime by the regulatory disclosure review workflow and the outcome is expected is deterministic

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat skills as executable code: scan for prompt injection and malicious scripts, and gate sensitive skills behind access control since skills can contain business logic and run scripts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some skills may have some prompts injection and skills actually does have scripts because that is the deterministic part of it

takeaways.technique: Governed workflow catalog, not just skills
takeaways.what_they_do: Apply the same registry/governance pattern to whole workflows (skills + subagents + hooks + MCP) so engineers reuse and improve workflows centrally rather than rebuilding them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to apply the same kind of like approach and solution for your whole workflows
